category_title: Collaborative students who adopt a teaching role to support their own learning
scenario_title: Avoiding digital summary strategies during independent reading
minimal_context: Jenna is working on an independent reading session using the Achieve 3000 program and is prompted to type a summary in the text box.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: It is time for independent reading. Please read the article on the Achieve 3000 program and type your response in the summary strategy text box.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I was just helping the new student learn to navigate through the reading program. Can I keep talking her through it instead?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You need to work independently right now. Please start your summary.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: But I already understand the story from our discussion earlier. I even showed my partner how to enlarge the text so we could read it better.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: That is fine, but you still need to use the summary strategy provided by the program.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I don't want to use the summary strategy. It is just too difficult and time consuming to type my responses into the text box.
